descriptionChirho: A high place of refuge or fortress, used as a metaphor for God's protection. All senses share the core meaning of an elevated stronghold or refuge. Multilingual evidence is uniform: Spanish 'refugio-alto' / 'baluarte' / 'refugio', Arabic 'malja' al-ali' (high refuge), Korean 'yosae' (fortress) / 'nop-eun pinanch'o' (high refuge), Swahili 'ngome' (fortress) / 'kimbilio' (refuge), Hindi 'garh' (fortress) / 'sharansthan' (refuge place) / 'unchai' (height). The grammatical variations (construct, pronominal suffixes 1cs/3ms, prepositional prefixes) do not alter the fundamental sense of a secure elevated place of defense or divine protection.
